metadata.title: Taxpayers' Guide to Education Spending (TGES) - Clifton Public Schools & Regional Peers
metadata.sourceAgency: New Jersey Department of Education (NJDOE) - Division of Finance

peerComparison.takeaway: Baseline: Above state median in administrative overhead ($1,890 vs $1,750 avg); 54.2% classroom instruction reflects significant mandated out-of-district tuition transfers ($24.9M).
Spends $145 less per pupil on administration and directs 2.6% more directly into classroom instruction; taxpayers fund 84% through local taxes due to minimal state aid.

Largest Passaic County district; highest per-pupil spending and highest legal/admin overhead; over 82% state aid funded.

budgetKeyInsights.title: Administrative Cost Gap
budgetKeyInsights.impact: Clifton spends $1,890 per pupil on administration vs. Bergen peer Fair Lawn at $1,695 per pupil. Across Clifton's 11,080 students, this $195/pupil difference equates to $2,160,600 in additional administrative overhead annually.

budgetKeyInsights.title: Classroom Instruction Share
budgetKeyInsights.impact: 54.2% of Clifton's budgetary spending is classified as direct classroom instruction, compared to an average of 57.3% among regional suburban peers. The gap is driven by $24.9M in out-of-district tuition transfers to specialized schools and county vocational institutes.

budgetKeyInsights.title: State Aid Vulnerability (S2 Formula)
budgetKeyInsights.impact: Clifton relies on NJ State Education Aid for 37.0% ($108.4M) of its budget. Because Clifton is classified as a low-wealth municipality under SFRA compared to Bergen/Morris peers (who receive ~10% state aid), any state formula adjustment has an outsized impact on local tax levies.
